notes: A clean Dragoon AF ladder that reads exactly as written. Bullets 2 and 3 are both Ceraulian and are merged -- consecutive talks on one NPC are one marker. Bullet 4 is split: getting a Kuftal Coffer Key is one thing you can be observed holding, opening the coffer is another and yields the [KI] Challenge to the Royal Knights, and both of the header's Item Reqs land as evidence that way. The coffer itself is deliberately unnamed: the page says only 'any coffer in Kuftal Tunnel' and never names the entity, so the target is none rather than a guessed 'Treasure Coffer'. Bullet 9 (find the ???) and bullet 10 (click it) are one examine; bullet 10's spawn and bullet 11's kill-then-check are a fight and a second examine, because the page really does say to click the same ??? again afterwards. The wyvern requirement is a spawn condition, not a step, and is carried as a note on the examine. Bullets 12 and 13 sit under the page's own 'Note:' heading and are explicitly 'not necessary', so they are optional epilogue talks. Drachen Armet is the header Reward and is not used as evidence. 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field and means false.

notes: Three real steps out of five bullets. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 is a daily lockout -- one Ward Warden / Desert Rain / Crimson Carpet per Vana'dielian day across all of Abyssea -- which nothing in the packets reports, so it is a flag and a note. Bullet 2 ('travel to the Target marked on your map') names no place at all: the trunk location is generated per run, so it merges into bullet 3's Repair Trunk rather than becoming a zone-less rung of its own, and that step keeps the zone but no grid. Bullet 3's long sub-bullet is packing advice -- sharp first, drop to round when the message changes, stop at 'about to reach the limit' -- and how full the sack is is not observable, so the only evidence in the quest is the [KI] Magicked hempen sack handed over at step 1. Bullet 5 is a Bastion outcome, not a step. Fame 'avun' is an Abyssea zone code, not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept.

bullet 2's 'Target marked on your map' has no fixed location on the page, so it merges here. Pack sharp material first, switch to round when the message changes and stop at 'about to reach the limit' -- overpacking tears the sack and fails the quest. How full it is is not observable.
the Cruor and Resistance Credits scale with how full the sack was

notes:
The whole quest is in the mangled wikitable at the top: the opening line 'Speak to Maat on a level 51 job' and the three-row Monster / Position / Key Item table are inside the [TABLE] block and carry no bullet numbers, so step 1 and the three collection steps have source_bullets [] or [1] and say so. The three frigicite are collected in any order, so they share a group and all three draw at once; because each cave yields a DIFFERENT key item, each step carries its own evidence without breaking the one-item-one-step rule, and the group shrinks as you collect. Since the February 2012 update the ??? at the far end of each cave always exists and gives the key item on touch, so the NMs need not be killed at all -- you can hold them, outrun them, or ride through the cave on a mount. ADVERSARY PASS: the three Boreal NMs were removed from mobs. role 'kill' asserts a kill the page explicitly denies ('you do not need to defeat the Notorious Monsters'), the corpus uses 'kill' only on fight steps and never on an examine, and the ??? already carries the marker and the grid, so the mob entry added nothing but a false instruction. Their names are kept in the step notes. Bullet 2 is Trust/Mount advice and not a step. The level 51 requirement is any job at 51, so jobs stays empty. All three frigicite resolve as key items and not as items.

notes:
The header names Hooknox as the giver but bullet 1 says only 'Enter Altar Room for a cutscene that starts this quest' -- there is nobody to talk to, so step 1 is a zone entry and Hooknox is kept in start only because the header claims her and the name is on the page; if she is a cutscene-only Goblin the marker simply never appears. Altar Room resolves as a zone of its own (Castle Oztroja's inner sanctum), and the sub-bullet route -- past the left/right switch gate with the trap door, out at (G-7), back into the castle, then (G-10) -- is travel advice, so it is a note. Bullets 2 and 3 stay separate steps on Ponono, as talk-then-trade always does, because only the second one needs items; the 10,000 gil is carried in the items list since gil resolves as an item. Bullet 4 is a game-day wait and then a talk, modelled as the talk with the wait in the note, since game time is not observable. Bullet 5's crafting recipe was stripped by the prepass, so the synthesis is one obtain step whose evidence is the Yagudo Headgear itself. Bullet 7 spawns seven NMs but only the Yagudo Avatar has to die, and bullet 8 is a second check of the same Stone Lid, so those are three steps on one object. Tsoo's Headgear is in the header Reward and so is NOT used as evidence at bullet 9 even though it is genuinely obtained mid-quest -- the hard rule wins and the note records the cost. The final step is a zone-out-and-back with Tsoo's Headgear equipped; the Gold Beastcoin is a reward.

notes: Four bullets, but bullet 3 is the whole quest and it forks. A dialogue choice at the past Offa sends you down either 'Somewhere in the City' (Markets > Markets (S) > Markets > Markets (S) trade > Markets > Markets (S) > Markets) or 'Conceal the burial spot with a Rock' (Markets > Markets (S) trade > Markets > Markets (S) > Markets); the choice itself is not observable and neither is any individual visit, so the branch is unmodelled and the shuttling is collapsed into one repeating_loop step whose note carries both orders verbatim. The recommended path is what the ladder is shaped to: a first return to present Offa, the Fish Bones trade to Offa (S), then the remaining alternation. The Rolanberry that ends bullet 3 would be the natural evidence for that loop, but it is in the header Reward, and it is also an ordinary AH fruit anyone might be carrying, so it is left out on both counts. Fish Bones is the header's Item Req and is the one honest evidence in the quest, though 'some Fish Bones' gives no count and 1 is assumed. Present and past Offa are one name in two zones; the past one is written 'Offa (S)' as the page writes it, which the normaliser folds to both the (S) and the plain key. Demoted to medium for the fork and the unstated visit counts. ADVERSARY PASS: the Fish Bones that are step 3's evidence are traded away at step 5, so the quest's one observable goes false again the moment it is used and the ladder drops back to the bottom for the whole second half. consumed_key_item belongs in review_flags and this pass may not add it; the ladder itself is unchanged and the quest stays medium, now for three reasons rather than two.

notes: Bullet 2 is not a step, it is what bullet 1 gives you, so it becomes step 1's evidence. Of the two key items only the [KI] Experiment cheat sheet is used: the [KI] Snoll reflector is plainly the thing that becomes the [KI] Frosted snoll reflector at the Impact Point (ids 1735 and 1736 sit next to each other), and an AND-list over both would read false the moment step 4 succeeds, exactly the trap As Thick as Thieves records. Bullet 4 is an observation about where the NM appears and bullet 6 is how to use it, so bullets 4 to 6 are one fight. That fight is unusual and the note says so: you attack the Frost Bomb Mk-II to RAISE its HP past 50%, then pull it to the Impact Point so it uses Hypothermal Combustion on the point -- role 'kill' is the closest the schema has to 'this is the thing you engage', and killing it is not the goal. Disengaging fails the quest outright. The 25-completions fame line, the reward table and the 'zoning is required to repeat' line are not steps. Fame 'aule' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing.

Attacking it RAISES its HP -- get it to at least 50% (higher pays more Cruor), then pull it onto the Impact Point, where it uses Hypothermal Combustion regardless of TP and damages the point, not you. Do NOT disengage: that fails the quest, which also makes Trusts risky if they take hate.

notes: Straight ladder, two zones, one real evidence point. Bullets 5 and 6 are the same Beastman Ensign twice in a row -- a cutscene then the click that opens the battlefield -- so they are one examine and the battlefield fight is split off, since a fight and an examine are not the same rung. The [KI] Flare grenade from bullet 4 is the quest's only observable, and it is carried as the items requirement on the Ensign step; the page never says it is consumed there, hence the flag rather than a second evidence claim. The replicas of Volker, Five Moons and Nicolaus are recorded only in the note: they are phases of the Arch Ahriman fight, the page says the battle can now end after a single Arch Ahriman without any of them appearing, and naming them as mobs would assert kills that may never happen. Everything under bullet 6 is tactics. The closing 'if you are working on missions then return to Crossroads of Time' is mission advice, not a step. Fame 'Wings of the Goddess' is not one of the nine regions, so it gates nothing and only raw is kept.

steps.note: just east of the bridge; the zone's Survival Guide or an Atmacite Refiner is the quickest way there

The Ahriman may vanish and put up replicas of Volker, Five Moons or Nicolaus in turn -- they are phases, not separate mobs, and since January 2021 the fight can end on a single Arch Ahriman with no replicas at all. Expect Sleepga II, Blindga and Poisonga II; easy at 99 with Trusts.
